newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: INTERVIEW-CHH'S FARACI SAYS NZ NEEDS MORE REFORM.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-CHH'S FARACI SAYS NZ NEEDS MORE REFORM.

text.p: Carter Holt Harvey Ltd chief executive John Faraci said New Zealand needed to recommence economic reform to rejuvenate its flat economy.
Faraci told the annual meeting the company's first quarter result reflected a weak New Zealand economy that was not growing at anywhere near the rate of previous years.
Growth was also well below what the government had forecast before last year's election, he said.

"What we need now is a firmer resolve by the governmwent to make restoration of economic growth a priority and to move forward with a reform agenda in those areas that will positively impact on our overall competitiveness," Faraci said.
The administration needed to reform the state's Accident Compensation Corporation, road transport, labour law, power generation and to privatise remaining assets.
"There are a lot of microeconomic reforms ... that have yet to be either completed or have yet to be started.
"All those things need to happen because the world isn't standing still," he said. "The economy is not growing at a rate that reflects its potential," he said.
Faraci said CHH was seeking a more transparency in road user charges to enable people to establish the most competitive transport system to use.
CHH, just over half owned by International Paper, last week reported a net profit of NZ$49 million in the first quarter to June, down from $56.0 million a year earlier.
